prerequisites: Physics 1: Forces and moments in space, their vector representation and vector sum/difference
Machine drawing: rules for drawing components and parts, dimensioning, understanding the drawing of parts and assemblies
Strength of materials/Solid mechanics: beam theory, calculating constraint reactions and internal forces, geometry of masses, stress calculations, resistance criteria
Applied physiscs: kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies
Metallurgy: naming steels and light alloys (symbols and meaning), material selection criteria in relation to the manufacturing process
Mechanical technology: manufacturing process in relation to the type and shape of the mechanical component to be manufactured

learning_outcomes.text: At the end of this course the student should know the basics of machine design.
He should gain understanding of the many factors affecting the design of mechanical parts with special regards to safety and reliability.
He should be familiar with design schemes and checks required to analyze machine parts.
He should be able to design a mechanical part on the basis of suitable material and process selection, load analysis and functional requirements.
He should be able to select from catalogues the main mechanical components found in machines.
He should be able to draw and dimension the part for production.
By the end of the course the student should be able to critically analyze machines and mechanical components and to their functions and requisites.
The student should be able to clearly present the functioning of mechanical devices and the design issues involved.

syllabus_topics: Factor of Safety with Statistical Reliability Concepts
Metallic Materials (Steel, Cast Iron, Aluminum, Magnesium, Titanium Alloys)
Application of the Beam Model in Mechanics
Stresses in Contact between Elementary Bodies
Mechanical power transmission: axles and shafts
Axles and shafts sizing and testing
Rolling bearings: choosing bearings from the catalog
Loose connections: screws, bolts, rivets, and nails
Loose connections: standards for threaded parts
Loose connections: load transmission by shear or friction
Loose connections: stiffness of parts and load distribution
Loose connections: testing in the presence of fatiguing loads
Fixed connections: technical standards for welding
Fixed connections: sizing of welded joints
Fixed connections: strength testing criteria for welding
Notes on sizing of glued joints
Pressure vessels under membrane conditions: standards
Pressure vessels: stress state in thin and thick vessels
teaching_methods: Numerical exercises carried out in the classroom
Problems proposed to be carried out at home with subsequent discussion in the classroom
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. Students must achieve a passing grade (18/30) in the written test to access the oral test. The grade for this module is a partial result and will count equally with the partial result of Module I to determine the final grade for Machine Design AB.
